# cleura_gardener_shoot_kubeconfig (Resource)

Requests a short-lived **admin kubeconfig** for a Gardener shoot cluster on Cleura
Cloud. On create the provider calls the Cleura API to issue a new admin credential
valid for `expiration_seconds`, and stores the resulting kubeconfig in the
(sensitive) `kubeconfig` attribute so it can be passed to the `kubernetes`/`helm`
providers or written out for `kubectl`.

The credential is **short-lived by design**. The provider rotates it by *replacing*
the resource — minting a brand-new kubeconfig — as it approaches expiry (see
[Credential lifecycle and rotation](#credential-lifecycle-and-rotation) below).

Attributes at a glance (the generated table further down lists types but carries no
per-attribute text — the schema has no descriptions yet):

- `shoot_name` *(Required, forces replacement)* — the shoot to issue the kubeconfig
  for. Changing it reissues the credential.
- `expiration_seconds` *(Required, forces replacement)* — requested validity of the
  minted credential, in seconds. Changing it reissues the credential.
- `renew_before_expiry_seconds` *(Optional, default `0`)* — how many seconds *before*
  expiry a Terraform run should proactively rotate the credential. Must stay **below**
  `expiration_seconds` (see the churn warning below).
- `kubeconfig` *(Read-only, sensitive)* — the minted admin kubeconfig. Stored in
  Terraform state; treat state as a secret.
- `expires_at` *(Read-only)* — RFC3339 timestamp at which the credential expires, as
  reported by the API when it was minted. Drives the rotation math; not something you set.
- `last_applied` *(Read-only, deprecated)* — RFC3339 timestamp of when the current
  kubeconfig was minted. Superseded by `expires_at`; still written, and still used to
  estimate expiry for resources whose state predates `expires_at`.

!> **Warning: destroying this resource does NOT revoke the credential.** `terraform
destroy` (or removing the resource) only drops the kubeconfig from Terraform state — it
makes **no** API call to Cleura. Any kubeconfig that was minted stays **valid on the
cluster until its own expiry** elapses. Keep `expiration_seconds` short, and rely on
expiry (not `destroy`) to bound a leaked credential's blast radius.

### Prerequisites

- The provider must be authenticated and scoped to the project that owns the shoot.
  Credentials resolve as **provider config > `CLEURA_*` env > the `cleura` CLI
  (`cleura login`)**; `region` and `project_id` are always taken from the provider
  configuration or environment, never from the CLI. See the provider's
  [Authentication](../index.md#authentication) documentation for the full setup.
- A `cleura_gardener_shoot` (or an existing shoot) whose `name` you pass to
  `shoot_name`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Fetch a short-lived admin kubeconfig for a shoot. The resource is recreated
# automatically once the credential reaches its renewal window.
resource "cleura_gardener_shoot_kubeconfig" "example" {
  # Name of an existing cluster. When the cluster is managed in the same
  # configuration, reference it instead so Terraform orders the two correctly:
  #   shoot_name = cleura_gardener_shoot.example.name
  shoot_name         = "example-cluster"
  expiration_seconds = 3600
}

output "kubeconfig" {
  value     = cleura_gardener_shoot_kubeconfig.example.kubeconfig
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Credential lifecycle and rotation

Rotation is driven entirely by Terraform runs — **there is no background timer or
controller.** The credential is only ever refreshed while you are running `terraform
plan`/`apply`.

On each run the provider computes, in wall-clock time and anchored to the expiry the API
reported when the credential was minted (`expires_at`):

```
renew_at = expires_at - renew_before_expiry_seconds
```

If `now > renew_at`, the provider marks the resource for replacement, emits a
`Kubeconfig expired` warning, and a fresh kubeconfig is minted on apply (the
`kubeconfig` value changes). Otherwise the existing credential is kept as-is.

Because rotation only happens on a run:

- If you never run Terraform, the kubeconfig is **never** rotated and simply expires on
  the cluster once `expiration_seconds` has elapsed.
- With the default `renew_before_expiry_seconds = 0`, `renew_at` equals the expiry
  moment, so rotation fires only **after** the credential has already expired. The
  kubeconfig in state can therefore be stale/expired until the next run rotates it.
  Set `renew_before_expiry_seconds` to a value **greater than 0** (for example `300`
  for a `3600`-second credential) to rotate *ahead* of expiry.

-> **Note:** `expires_at` is the expiry the **API granted**, not the one you requested,
so rotation stays correct even when Cleura clamps or shortens `expiration_seconds`.
Resources created before the provider recorded `expires_at` still estimate expiry from
`last_applied` plus the requested `expiration_seconds`; they move onto the API's own
answer the first time they rotate. Upgrading does not itself rotate anything.

~> **Warning — replacement churn footgun:** keep `renew_before_expiry_seconds` strictly
**below** `expiration_seconds`. If `renew_before_expiry_seconds >= expiration_seconds`,
then `renew_at` falls at or before the moment the credential was minted, so the renewal
window is already open and the resource is **replaced on every single apply** — minting
(and leaking, per the destroy note above) a new credential each time.

## Import

Import is **intentionally unsupported** — the resource does not implement import. There
is no durable server-side object to adopt into state: each apply mints a brand-new
credential, and the kubeconfig body (with its private key material) is only returned at
issue time and cannot be re-read afterwards. To (re)create a managed kubeconfig, add the
resource to your configuration and `terraform apply`.

## Schema

### Required

- `expiration_seconds` (Number) Requested validity of the issued kubeconfig, in seconds from when it is minted. Changing it forces replacement so a new kubeconfig can be issued with the new lifetime.
- `shoot_name` (String) Name of the Gardener shoot cluster to issue the admin kubeconfig for. Changing it forces replacement, because the kubeconfig is only minted at creation and is not regenerated on update.

### Optional

- `renew_before_expiry_seconds` (Number) Seconds before the kubeconfig's expiry at which Terraform proactively rotates it (by replacing the resource on the next plan/apply). Must be less than expiration_seconds. Defaults to 0, meaning the kubeconfig is rotated only after it has fully expired.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) RFC3339 timestamp at which the kubeconfig expires, as reported by the API when it was minted. Drives rotation together with renew_before_expiry_seconds.
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) The generated administrator kubeconfig for the shoot cluster, rendered as YAML. This is the full admin credential and is marked sensitive.
- `last_applied` (String, Deprecated) Deprecated: use expires_at. RFC3339 timestamp recording when the kubeconfig was issued, from which the provider used to estimate expiry before the API returned it. Still written, and still used for resources whose state predates expires_at.
